title: Reusable QUBO-Derived Block-Schur Inverse Factors for Fixed-Operator Finite-Difference PDE Solvers
authors: Arash Fath Lipaei, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu, Özlem Salehi, Selin Aslan
abstract: Many simulations of partial differential equations require the repeated solution of linear systems whose matrix remains fixed while the righthand side changes. We present a hybrid offline online framework for this setting. The discretized operator is organized into small coupled blocks and reduced through block Schur complements. Instead of expressing the complete PDE solution as one large binary optimization problem, quadratic unconstrained binary optimization is used only to construct reusable local inverse factors. These factors are computed during an offline stage, decoded and stored, and then reused in an ordinary classical block solve for subsequent righthand sides. The optimizer facing problem size is governed by the local block size and chosen numerical precision, rather than by the dimension of the full spatial grid. We develop the mathematical formulation, analyze the accuracy and resource requirements of the binary representation, and examine the method on representative finite difference PDE problems, including execution of the local optimization stage on quantum optimization hardware. The resulting architecture provides a reusable interface between conventional numerical linear algebra and QUBO based quantum optimization.
summary: This paper introduces a hybrid offline-online framework to solve PDEs by leveraging quantum optimization. It uses QUBOs only in an offline stage to pre-calculate reusable local inverse factors derived from the PDE operator structure. These factors are then used in a fast, classical block-solve routine for any subsequent right-hand side, significantly reducing the quantum computational burden.
main_problem: Developing a reusable framework to solve linear systems arising from fixed-operator Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) where the right-hand side changes repeatedly.
main_result: The authors propose an architecture that separates the operator-dependent preprocessing (offline) from the repeated solves (online), allowing QUBO optimization to run only once.
method: The method uses block-Schur decomposition to reduce the PDE system into local blocks, whose inverse factors are constructed by solving least-squares problems formulated as QUBOs during an offline stage.
model_or_system: The model involves discretizing PDEs (like Heat or Poisson) into large linear systems ($Ax=b$), which are then decomposed into block-tridiagonal structures suitable for Schur recursion.
key_observables: Local inverse residuals, global solution error ($\lVert A\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{b} Vert$), and the normalized objective gap ($g_j$).
important_parameters: The computational cost is governed by the local block size, not the full spatial grid dimension. Resolution is controlled by the fixed-point precision $K$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the ability to separate the problem into local blocks and that the required inverse columns can be accurately represented by a QUBO formulation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the offline-online architecture. Figure 6 audits the reconstruction of inverse columns from QUBO submissions, showing residual ratios. Figure 7 shows end-to-end PDE reconstructions using cached factors for Heat, Poisson, and Klein-Gordon equations.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for a reusable solver for fixed-operator PDEs. It then details the mathematical formulation using block-Schur decomposition and reformulates the inverse factor calculation as a QUBO problem. The core contribution is the hybrid offline-online framework, followed by analysis and testing on representative PDEs.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the interface between classical numerical linear algebra (PDE solvers) and quantum optimization (QUBO), providing a concrete, reusable quantum kernel for scientific computing.

For a fixed finite-difference operator, the block-tridiagonal organization is reduced to Schur blocks and each required inverse column is represented as a signed fixed-point least-squares QUBO. The decoded columns are assembled into approximate Schur inverses and cached. Coupling factors may either be cached explicitly or evaluated from the cached inverse factors during substitution.
